questions.q: prices = np.array([20.0, 55.5, 130.0, 8.25, 42.0]). What does prices[1:4] return?
questions.explain: A slice starts at index 1 and stops just before index 4, so it returns the elements at positions 1, 2 and 3.

questions.q: You run sl = prices[1:3] and then sl[0] = 99.0. What happens to prices?
options: prices[1] also becomes 99.0, because a basic slice is a view of the same data
Nothing, because slicing always copies the data
NumPy raises an error because slices are read-only
The whole prices array is replaced by sl
questions.explain: Basic slices are views, not copies. Use .copy() when you need an independent array.

questions.q: For a 2D array m, what does m[:, 1] select?
options: The element in row 1 and column 1
The second column, from every row
questions.explain: The first position is rows and the second is columns. A colon means all rows, so m[:, 1] is the column at index 1.

questions.q: Which pair of shapes can NumPy broadcast together?
questions.explain: Shapes are compared from the right. (2, 3) and (3,) match on the last dimension (3 and 3), and the missing dimension counts as 1.

questions.q: a = np.array([3, -1, 4, -5]). What does a[a < 0] = 0 do?
options: Sets every negative element to 0, leaving a as [3, 0, 4, 0]
Returns a new array of only the negative values and leaves a unchanged
Raises an error because a comparison cannot be used to assign
questions.explain: A boolean mask can be used on the left side of an assignment; every position where the mask is True receives the value.
